businessModel: Funded by Kagi search subscribers; free browser with optional Orion+ ($5/mo, $50/yr, $150 lifetime)
updateCadence: iOS roughly every 2-4 weeks (1.5.4 Sep 17, 1.5.5 Oct 1, 2026); macOS point releases
summary: Kagi's zero-telemetry WebKit browser for macOS and iOS: runs Safari, Chrome and Firefox extensions (~70% of WebExtensions API), built-in ad blocking and Kagi Search. Linux and Windows efforts were stopped in Oct 2026.
bestFor: Mac/iPhone users who want extensions beyond Safari
People wanting a no-telemetry Apple-native browser
notFor: Windows or Linux users (Kagi stopped development)
People wanting open source on Apple platforms

pros.title: Chrome/Firefox extensions on WebKit
pros.detail: Kagi claims 150,000+ extensions via roughly 70% of the WebExtensions API, including on iOS.

cons.title: Linux/Windows dropped
cons.detail: Kagi ended development on Oct 2, 2026; community handoff uncertain.

faq.q: What happened to Orion for Linux and Windows?
faq.a: Kagi ended its development on 2026-10-02; the Linux beta keeps working without updates and the source is to be open-sourced for the community.
Yes; Orion+ is an optional paid tier ($5/mo, $50/yr, $150 lifetime).
No. It is WebKit-based on macOS and iOS (WebKitGTK on the Linux beta).

timeline.event: Orion begins as a Kagi project
Kagi ends Linux/Windows development (Oct 2) and iOS 1.5.5 ships (Oct 1)

switching.note: Imports from Safari, Chrome and Firefox.
